problem: Prior work evaluates navigation approaches in isolation, so there is no unified comparison of classical versus deep-learning, VLN and foundation-model navigators across different domains, nor guidance on sim-to-real, robustness and explainability.
motivation: Autonomous navigation in unstructured, dynamic, semantically rich environments needs perception, mapping, planning and control under latency, energy and safety constraints. Classical SLAM+A*/RRT stacks struggle in dynamic and semantic scenes, while learned approaches raise sim-to-real, robustness and explainability concerns. A cross-domain benchmark is needed to compare them.
key_idea: Benchmark eight AI navigation systems (DRL, modular DL, occupancy CNN, NavTransformer, VLN-BERT, LangNav, Neural SLAM, NavGPT) across four navigation domains and propose a deployment-readiness framework covering safety, robustness and explainability.
insight: Per the abstract, the best system depends on the domain: NavTransformer leads structured indoor navigation and LangNav leads instruction-following. Modular deep learning transfers best from sim to real (8.4pp SR gap vs 24.2pp for end-to-end DRL), suggesting that keeping classical planning components helps deployment. Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited.
method: Systems benchmarked: end-to-end DRL, modular DL (perception + classical planning), occupancy map CNN, NavTransformer, VLN-BERT, LangNav (language-conditioned RL), Neural SLAM, NavGPT (foundation model).
Domains: indoor structured, outdoor unstructured terrain, dynamic pedestrian-dense scenes, and semantically complex instruction-following navigation.
Evaluation platforms: iGibson 2.0 simulator, Habitat challenge benchmark, real-world corridor trials at two European robotics labs, and the R2R dataset.
Sim-to-real analysis: success-rate gap between simulation and real-world trials per system.
Deployment readiness framework: criteria covering safety, robustness and explainability for AI navigation systems.

setting.backbone: Benchmark of eight systems: DRL, modular DL, occupancy CNN, NavTransformer, VLN-BERT, LangNav, Neural SLAM, NavGPT

numbers_note: abstract only; the abstract reports NavTransformer 84.6% SR on structured indoor navigation, LangNav 72.4% on instruction-following, and sim-to-real SR gaps of 8.4pp (modular DL) vs 24.2pp (end-to-end DRL), but these are not tied to a specific benchmark split or metric table, so they are not recorded as numbers entries.
results: NavTransformer achieves the highest success rate on structured indoor navigation (84.6%), LangNav leads semantic instruction-following (72.4%), and modular deep learning has the smallest sim-to-real gap (8.4pp vs 24.2pp for end-to-end DRL).
limitations: Only an abstract was available, so protocol details, splits and baselines are unknown.
This is a benchmark and survey-style study rather than a new method, and the abstract gives no per-benchmark, split-level metrics.
